title: Bayern beats Union Berlin in Bundesliga opener
seoTitle: Bayern beats Union Berlin in Bundesliga opener
subtitle: The opening match of the new season marked the debut of coach Marie-Louise Eta and set an attendance record.
excerpt: FC Bayern München defeated 1. FC Union Berlin 4-1 in the opening match of the new Bundesliga season, drawing a large crowd.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
FC Bayern München kicked off the new Bundesliga season with a 4-1 away victory over 1. FC Union Berlin. The match marked the start of the competition's 37th season and was played in front of a record crowd of 17,083 spectators at the Stadion An der Alten Försterei.

How the opening match unfolded

The visiting team secured the triumph with goals from Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder, Glodis Perla Viggosdottir, and Sophie Proost. For Union Berlin, player Nele Bauereisen narrowed the scoreline in the final stretch of the match. The home side created the first major chance of the clash through Eileen Campbell, but Bayern capitalized on their technical superiority as the game progressed.

Union Berlin's debut and objectives

The match marked the official debut of new head coach Marie-Louise Eta in charge of Union Berlin. The team fielded four newly signed players from the start, including Lisanne Gräwe, Jella Veit, Jill Janssens, and Leela Egli. Despite the defeat against the reigning champions, the coach highlighted the positive aspects of the team's performance against a top-tier opponent.

Bayern's unbeaten streak

With the positive result in Berlin, Bayern reached the milestone of 20 consecutive away wins. The team also extended its run to 43 matches without defeat in the national tournament, coming close to equaling its own historical record of 44 unbeaten games set between 2022 and 2024.

Statements on the importance of star players

Before the start of the round, forward Klara Bühl emphasized the significance of keeping standout players in the German league to ensure the competition's attractiveness and competitiveness. This year's women's championship features the distinct characteristic of having exclusively clubs backed by men's teams, generating positive expectations for long-term development.

With information from OneFootball, DFB, BILD.
